locator: The Unreality of Time, conclusion: 'Whenever we judge anything to exist in time, we are in error'
interpretation: McTaggart argues that time involves change, that the only change is change of an event's A-series determinations (past, present, future), and that the A series is contradictory; so no event really changes, and whenever we judge or perceive anything as in time we judge or perceive it as it is not. Read as: no event changes in its A-series determinations, and there are judgings and perceivings. The claim keeps his own sense of change (DISAMB-CHANGE-A-SERIES); it does not say that nothing is reduced from potency to act, which would need the unattributed bridge STMT-BEING-MOVED-INVOLVES-A-SERIES-CHANGE. The final paragraph raises the retorsion itself ('must it not be to an appearance which changes ... and is not time, then, shown to be real after all?') and promises an answer; the answer (The Nature of Existence II, ch. XLIV, § 511) is the separate claim MCTAGGART-NOE-II-511-APPEARINGS-DO-NOT-CHANGE-A.
